I wish there was a sideways thumb for this. It's not a bad game. There's just not $8 worth of content here. I finished the entire game in about an hour and a half. I probably could have beaten it sooner if I invested more in oxygen. It shows 4.5 hours because I left the game running in the background for a couple hours. Once you beat the main game, you unlock endless mode. Compared to other incremental games, the branching skill tree is tiny. Lots of upgrades I thought I would eventually see but never saw such as card drops being drawn to my ship, lasers shooting behind me, faster attack speeds, landmines, turrets (although mothership sort of is one) and just crazier and crazier upgrades to deal with the more challenging encounters I would face with each passing wave. But it never came. I beat all 15 waves and that was it. I was only half way done with the skill tree. The balance just seems off when it comes to progression. I also found the game incredibly easy once you unlocked the double laser upgrade. The game is way too short even as an incremental game. The end screen made it seem like more stuff was on the way so maybe the game will get better. I'd love to see a bigger branching tree with upgrades that look cool and feel good to use, actual boss battles that really challenge you, and more waves. All in all, it's not a bad game. Just lacking content.
升级的东西太少了

Void Miner is a decent enough game, but I would not recommend it primarily because of my frustration with the run timer mechanic (oxygen). 90+% of my runs ended due to oxygen running out, and since the only way to get more oxygen during a run is based on RNG that means that every run it was a toss up how far I would make it. I would point to Astro Prospector for a better way of handling mid-run buffs and drops.

A decent little game. I would give it a neutral score, but as that's not possible, I'll slightly lean into a non-recommendation. It gives the impression it's more a game-jam or a learning project than an actual developed game for the public. While playing I couldn't help but think of little details that could be improved a ton with only minor effort; - The tiny white crosshair often went missing in all the chaos. - Picking up chips/temporary upgrades does not show what kind of upgrade it gives at the point of pick-up, it just stealthily gets added at the bottom of the screen. - The enemy ship movement and shooting is extremnely straightforward; think 90ies era 'just strafe around the enemy to dodge everything' pushing every encounter towards the corner of the screen - The sound effect of the missile launcher is quite a loud and repetitive noise, almost nullifying all the other sound effects/sound track. There's a lot of low hanging fruit here. I'm sure it's a good learning experience for the developer though, and I see potential there.
barely anything here. 3.5 hrs for all content and unlocks. hope more is added.

This is a neat little game, it feels like a completed school project with a bit of extra love. It's not a great game but for an indie game, specifically if it's a first attempt at making a game at all, it's still respectable. The game needs a lot of improvements to be good, most of all accessability, it's not very easy to follow the ship or distinguish the collected money from enemy bullets, and the game lacks a bit of soul. I Hope you keep trying to make games. You seem to have technical know-how to do better than this, and I'd like to see it.
It's been an hour and a half since I've seen my mouse cursor, I hope it's doing well wherever it is

Played this game for a few hours, didn't quite finish, but it was very mediocre as far as these short incremental games go. No real interesting ideas, the upgrade tree is pretty uninspired, and overall it's just "okay" at best. But then I discovered that this game was developed using generative AI that isn't disclosed in any way on Steam, despite this being a requirement. In fact, not only was it not disclosed, but the developer bans and removes comments from anyone discussing it, so they're actively trying to hide this fact to trick people into buying their worthless slop. ♥♥♥♥ generative AI, and ♥♥♥♥ developers who use it, especially without disclosing it. Hope this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ gets removed from Steam for breaking the rules deliberately and flagrantly.

2026年2月24日，成就通关了点击增量游戏《虚空矿工》，大约8小时。这是一款制作非常粗糙的游戏，游戏画面大约是15年前的水准，游戏玩法至少也是10年前的水准了。整个游戏没有剧情，UI设计水平还不如Word，大约是写字板的程度，尽管在结局中，制作人发自肺腑地表示自己编程多年，制作游戏依然举步维艰，但是这难以掩盖这款游戏过于简陋的事实。在玩法上，有母舰、激光、炮台、炸弹等诸多形式，敌人的类型也有所变化。但实际上除了移动和躲子弹攒钱升级之外，并没多少可以做的事情。我是挂机了一段时间所以通关用时比较长，如果一直手动操作的话，3小时可以全成就。
谢谢nob老师送的游戏！！这是个中评 -制作很粗糙，像15年的手游水平，看着很像ppt。 -emmm字体真的很丑阿？？怎么设计的 -性价比真的很低，我觉得几块钱差不多 游戏玩法是移动和躲子弹攒钱升级，中规中矩的增量游戏，到后期也没有那么爽。 +全成就速度很快，3h左右就可以全成就，没有刁难的成就。

I can't recommend this game with any enthusiasm. While I appreciate what the developer went through to create this game, it was frustrating more than fun. There's so much going on screen at once, that's it's easy to lose your crosshair, and have no idea what you're aiming at. That leads to taking damage and losing progress on your run. The concept is great, but the UI could use improvement.

I do like to play idle/incremental games, because, even with the repetitiveness that comes with the genre, there's that progression addictive gameplay that keeps you hooked. Here, all feels the same. And the core gameplay is just something basic that reminds you of really old games (and not in a good way). Change the background to slightly different color, random meteors show up, pew pew pew, same ships show up in the same pattern, pew pew, and so on. At no point i felt like the gameplay was enjoyable nor that i was getting consistently stronger.

not really even an incremental game, just alot of useless upgrades. there is absolutely no visual clarity. no point in picking up money because it just auto collects when you kill enemies. there is no sound effect for taking damage so some times you dont realize when you are starting to die. I do really like that you can pick up node upgrades in a run though. 2/10 incremental but maybe a 4/10 game.

I can't give this a good review because: - If I unlock every upgrade available and still can't finish the game after multiple tries, it's too hard. - The control scheme is lacking. - Ship and cursor visibility are lacking. I can't tell if my ship is failing to turn because I am not pointing at an enemy of if the ship just isn't turning when I do point at an enemy. But seriously, I can't finish the achievements as long as I can't finish the game and I can't finish the game even with every possible unlock so I just can't endorse this. Not at any price. Edit: I'd like to thank the person who awarded a "funny" award to my review. I'm sure you can imagine how that impacts my likelihood to change my review!

This game isn't necessarily bad, but I was already bored after finishing my second run (less than 10 minutes in), which is not a very good outlook for any game. The upgrades don't really change anything (the mothership is an interesting idea, but it kinda just dies without doing much) and the gameplay stays the exact same throughout the entirety of the game. You don't get to chase much bigger asteroids, different kinds of asteroids or anything of the sort. You only ever get one material for upgrades and that's it. As for the controls, I understand why the sliding is there, but it made the game extremely annoying to play. On top of that, asteroids can spawn off-screen right next to you when you were near the border. The playtime is only about 2.5 hours to 100%. I got the game in a bundle, but can't recommend it to anyone. There's much better incremental games for the same price or even cheaper, and the playtime of a lot of them is also longer. I can't give this one a thumbs up in good faith.

Overall> This game feels like the most generic asteroid shooter ever, the one that you often develop as a part of game design tutorials. Honestly, it may as well be aa student project, not a comercial game. Gameplay> It has no interesting mechanics, specific upgrades individually have almost no impact, good upgrades are actually hidden in a tree behind absolutely useless ones. Gaphically> One level, 3 asteroids (just resized versions of 1 asteroid), 3 enemies.

Progress feels a bit slow in the beginning and then after 2-3h WTF i have already reached the end of of one part of the unlock tree? Ok there must be more when i unlock the top half..... aaaaaand 2h later. NOPE. Its neat, but short, repeating even for an incremental game, probably because of lack up upgrades. The price does not nearly match the content, i think the real play time is like 4h, i let the game run when i was afk.

EDIT: Just learned that generative AI was used to create the soundtrack so I'm changing my recommendation. It's a shame too because the game is pretty fun, generative AI is hot garbage that shouldn't be encouraged. Dude, heh, I didn't know what all to expect going into this game but I definitely didn't expect a soundtrack that slaps harder than it has any reason to. The game is damn fun as is but the music perked my ears right up. A lot of it reminds me of Kung Fury and I'm all about it. A++ 🤘🏻

Its hard for me to not recommend it, but it has so many little issues that add up to make it really hard to play. Firstly, both control schemes suck. One is supposed to harken back to the old days, but it just feels wrong, so was forced to play with the default controls. Only way I could do so was to ignore my ship, which meant that I bumped into things a lot. Because the default controls facing direction doesn't matter for movement. So its basically a turret that moves. Very confusing for me, and struggled to play the entire game as a result. Secondly, too many projectiles on the screen that look too much like my ship. I'm looking at you Orbs. Its so chaotic that I lose my crosshair constantly and my ship's position as well. Doesn't help that you can go up and appear at the down area, which causes more confusion than it resolves. Thirdly, the progression is total crud. I had to buy out 95% of the tree in order to beat the game. And the endless mode is supposed to give you the money to complete the tree, but I didn't need it at all, and once you unlock all the oxygen, there is no endless progression options. Fourth, gameplay was too similar with each loop, but what determined success was largely if enough bonus oxygen shows up, or medkits when you take hits. Otherwise, there isn't any strategy to it. I never found the need to use the Dash, as it just made controlling the ship worse and your speed is often too fast already. ===== The only real saving grace was the soundtrack. Huge variety, great audio, and fits the game's theme perfectly. I just wish everything else was as good. Without the soundtrack, I likely would have given up on it. I feel bad for negatively reviewing the game, as the developer struggled to produce it, but, for someone who has coded for half their life, the game's code is highly unstable. Input delays, lost inputs, a game crash, missiles that pass through enemies, missiles that don't home in and go dumbfire for reasons, the ship sometimes faced a different direction than I had intended, and many other small irritating things, that just shows me that they still don't know what they are doing. How is it that with demo testers, playtesters, and others that this all failed to be noticed and ended up in v1.0? Is it laziness, or incompetence? I don't like to cast shade on other fledging game devs, but the amount of issues I had while playing tells me either they ignored their playtesters, or they rushed the game to release and abandoned it shortly thereafter.

This game is fairly shallow and deeply un-satisfying to play. I'm starting to get jaded by all of these "Incremental" games that last just over 2h and end with little effort put into them. Your growth is stagnant throughout the entire run, a run at 15m and a run at 2h give almost identical rewards. The mechanic itself is extremely easy and you will run out of time infinitely more than you run out of health, which means despite having an activity to do most of the game is just waiting. It ends extremely unceremoniously with no climactic battle or fanfare. Frankly I just don't understand why a game in this state was released, and why people who enjoy this genre would recommend it despite it being so deeply flawed.

- 虽然给了推荐，但请慎重购买。 - 全成就游玩时间：4 小时，其中有 1 小时是低效率的玩手机挂机刷钱，如果是专注玩可能不到 3 小时就能全成就。 - 游戏玩法： - 很简单，简单说就是纯玩局外成长。 - 就是一个固定的 15 关。一开始玩家很弱，可能第一关都过不了，但是能打点钱，打了钱能给自己升级升科技，反复挑战，最后打过 15 关，你就全成就了。 - 购买建议：只建议打骨折或随其他游戏大包一起购买。 - 理由： - 内容量太少、小游戏级别、玩法简单、毫无难度、重复游玩价值低。 - 作者在通关时表达了这个游戏项目有多困难，可以看出来是一个练手级别的项目。 - 缺点： - 难度可以说是极低，因为只要不断局外成长就行，其他都无所谓的。中期可以挂机刷钱。 - 内容量少，游戏的美术音乐资产就那几个。 - 视觉疲劳，游戏后期屏幕太乱，基本上不靠操作，乱拳打死就行了。
The game is pretty fun but the upgrade interface mouse controls were horrible, my mouse slid all over the place like it was on ice, this behavior didn't appear during normal gameplay however.
1.游戏内容解锁缓慢，大量重复内容。 2.不能用CE修改器。 3.升级体验不明显，资源获取极度缓慢。 4.游戏UI简陋。 5.后期满屏子弹和怪，经常找不到自己位置。 结论;一款不增量的增量游戏，不肉鸽的肉鸽游戏，没有自动瞄准纯手动不休闲的游戏，不及格的作品。

Neat little asteroids game, basically the same as the 'original' asteroids but modernised. Well done to the dev on their first game! My only issues are: a) The menu settings do not persist throughout the gameplay, b) there's no save mid-round, so if you need to leave you lose all progress, and c) there's really not that much content here.
a fun little game. i enjoyed the 2 hours or so with it.

Had a good time playing through to the end and getting all the upgrades. I think it slows down a bit towards the end of the game and suffers from visual chaos, but blowing up enemies and asteroids remains fun through to the end.

This feels like a flash game I would’ve been playing in school between essays and tests and I mean that in a positive way. It captured a feeling from that time in its visuals and gameplay very well. It’s not a very deep game in its mechanics or in the gameplay but if you’re looking for something chill to kill time with this is a great choice. Perfect Deck game, I feel like it may not be as enjoyable as on an actual computer. The ability to pick it up and play a few rounds for a bit and move on made this a very enjoyable experience but it might not hit the same otherwise.

Honestly, this game is pretty good. I think that the game is lacking a bit for its price but that can easily be fixed. If you're looking for a nice, short, and satisfying game to play, this is the game for you. The music for this game is AMAZING!!! You can really hear the effort put into it and the music fits PERFECTLY with the game. Some things that I think the game could add/change to make it more worth the price are: - Make the cards stand out more against the background since they are tiny and can easily blend in - Adding more achievements since they feel underwhelming - Adding a menu option for when you are in a run to end the run early and keep the things you've collected since if I had an upgrade I wanted to get and I was a few gems short, I would have to start a run and once I got enough, purposefully die (which can take a good few seconds) Ignoring all of those things, I honestly thing that this is a pretty good game and as I said before, you should get it if you are looking for a nice, short, and satisfying game to play.
Very fun and reminiscent of Lyca. I love the music and the feel of flying

Calling this game a roguelite is a bit generous, this is more like this kind of a flash game where you play a round, die, earn some currency, and then buy upgrades which will let you progress farther in the next round. An upgrade-a-thon how I like to call it. Yeah, in all regards, this game is not that far away from a flash game, or more like, an HTML5 game from mid-2010, the only exception is that those games were free and this one is like $5. There's no story, not even a paragraph of it, the graphics are a mishmash of pixelart-ey sprites of different resolutions and from different sources, and the gameplay, as basic as it is, is quite janky, like, not much consideration was given to make the few mechanics this game's got as perfect as they could be. Normally I'd give this game a negative review, but I did willingly beat this game like 4 or so times, so it'd be disingenuous of me if I did. Perhaps that was an accidental genius, I certainly am not gonna credit the developer with implementing it this way intentionally, but this game allows for beating it with different builds. Like, normally, and during your first playthrough, you would generally strive to buy every upgrade, but there's one upgrade which benefits from having less overall upgrades bought - the upgrade which enables random drops of improvements for the upgrades you bought which last for the duration of the round, and so if you spread your upgrades out, there'd be less chances of one singular upgrade to grow to a ridiculous degree and potentially make it overpowered. And so I replayed the game multiple times, trying different builds, seeing what works and what doesn't. It just so happens to be a specific instance of jank I enjoy, and as I said, I very much doubt this was implemented intentionally, so decide for yourself if you want to spend 5-ish dollars for a slapdash clone of Asteroids

Starts a little slow but when you start powering up, it makes you feel powerful but frantic enough you never feel invincible. Worth the purchase!

This game was good fun. It is worth the price, but there is a lack of endgame content. There are many upgrades and unlocks that keep the game decently interesting. The problem is, it ends a bit quickly. I 100%ed the game in less than 3 hours. All they offer is an endless mode, which I understand they can't add much more to when you beat the game, but there's no real motive to continue. Overall worth it, but it doesn't offer much at the end.
